## Rationale

`pm get --at <version|timestamp>` (pm-hib1, shipped PR#549) proves single-item reconstruction works. The workspace-level twin does not exist, and the product says so in its own source:

- `src/cli/commands/get.ts:384` — "Get --at cannot be combined with --tree because workspace-level historical projections are not yet indexed."
- `src/cli/commands/get.ts:465` — "Get --at cannot project children because workspace-level historical relationships are not yet indexed."

Measured 2026-07-25: `--at` appears in exactly two flag-contract entries (`flag-contracts.ts:920`, `:1497`); `pm list --at` exits with `Unknown option --at`.

The immutable history guarantee is only half-delivered while the answer to "what did this project look like on 2026-03-01" requires replaying 2,032 streams by hand. Full-proof restoration is an item-scoped promise today and a portfolio-scoped promise in the mandate.

## Scope

One historical projection primitive in the SDK, consumed by every read surface:

1. `projectWorkspaceAt(ts | version-vector)` — reconstructs the item set, field values, and relationship edges valid at an instant, from history streams plus a bounded cached snapshot ladder.
2. `--at` accepted uniformly on `list`, `search`, `context`, `deps`, `graph`, and `get --tree` (the two refusals above become real support).
3. Reads under `--at` stay immutable: no usage-ledger write, no claim side effects, no index mutation beyond the read cache — the `pm get --at` precedent.
4. Bounded cost: projection uses checkpoint snapshots plus tail replay, so cost scales with events-since-checkpoint, not with total history. Interacts with `pm history-compact` baselines — a compacted stream must still project correctly (its synthetic baseline is a legitimate checkpoint).

## Why this is a platform primitive, not a reporting nicety

- Forensics: "which items were open when the release cut" answered from data, not memory.
- Provable history (pm-w7ccmv): a third party can re-derive any past portfolio state and compare against an attestation bundle (pm-3z0k).
- Domain platform (pm-t4d7nz): a VCS or digital-twin domain built on pm primitives needs "state at revision" as a first-class read, not a per-item loop.
- Delta reads (pm-tuadp2) are the forward-difference twin: `--since <cursor>` answers "what changed", `--at <ts>` answers "what was true". Same projection machinery, opposite direction.

## Phasing

1. SDK projection primitive + checkpoint ladder + conformance replay gate.
2. `list`/`deps`/`get --tree` surfaces (removes the two documented refusals).
3. `context`/`search`/`graph` under `--at` (relevance scoring against historical candidate sets).
4. Scale hardening against the pm-801d read index and pm-0qg5 storage fan-out.
Workspace-level point-in-time projection: every read surface answers what the project looked like at time T from history alone

Promote the single-item pm get --at reconstruction to a workspace-scoped SDK projection primitive consumed by list, search, context, deps, graph, and get --tree, so any past portfolio state is re-derivable from immutable history without hand-replaying streams.

A public SDK primitive reconstructs the item set, field values, and relationship edges valid at any timestamp or version from history streams plus checkpoint snapshots; --at is accepted on list, search, context, deps, graph, and get --tree with one shared flag contract; the two documented refusals in get.ts (--tree and children projections) are replaced by working support; reads under --at perform zero mutations including usage-ledger writes; a replay gate asserts projected state equals independently recorded state at N past instants including across a history-compact baseline; projection cost is bounded by events-since-checkpoint, not total history; docs cover forensic and audit usage
